name: Plainclause Store Vacation & Holiday Mode for WooCommerce
author: plainclause

sections.description:
Going on holiday, moving stock or just need a break? Put your WooCommerce shop in vacation mode without hiding it. Products stay visible (and keep their search rankings), customers see a clear notice with your reopening date, and the shop opens again by itself.

Set the dates once under WooCommerce > Settings > Store hours and forget about it: the shop closes at the start time, shows “Our shop is closed until 9 November, 9:00”, and reopens on time. No coming-back-to-untick-a-box, no lost customers who think the shop is gone.

Why this one

  • Scheduled, not just on/off. Set the start and end date and time in advance; it closes and reopens on its own, in your site’s time zone.
  • Tell customers before you go. Show “Heads up: we’ll be closed from … until …” a few days ahead, so regulars can order in time.
  • Nothing slips through. Add to cart is paused on product pages, and items already in carts cannot be checked out, including with the checkout block.
  • Keep some things on sale. Leave chosen categories purchasable, such as gift cards or downloads.
  • Lightweight and private. No external services, no tracking, no nag screens.

Features

  • Close the shop now with one tick, or schedule a vacation with a start and end date and time.
  • Reopens automatically at the end time.
  • Products stay visible; “Add to cart” is paused and items already in carts cannot be checked out.
  • Notice banner with the reopening date ({reopen}), on every page or only on shop pages, or anywhere with the [pcsh_notice] shortcode.
  • Announce a vacation in advance: show “we’ll be closed from … until …” a few days before.
  • “Notice only” mode: keep taking orders and just tell customers that orders ship after you return.
  • Keep chosen categories purchasable (for example gift cards or downloads).
  • Works with the cart and checkout blocks and classic themes.
  • No external services, no tracking.

Pro add-on (optional)

Everything above is free and stays free. A separate paid add-on adds:

  • Weekly opening hours, for example Monday to Friday 9:00 to 17:00, including hours past midnight.
  • Any number of planned closures (public holidays, stocktake days), each with its own message.

Plainclause Store Hours Pro costs from $19 a year for one site, with a 30-day money-back guarantee. It is sold by Freemius, our reseller and merchant of record.

More from Plainclause

  • Plainclause Sequential Order Numbers for WooCommerce: clean, gap-free order numbers with your own prefix.
  • Plainclause EU Withdrawal Button & Legal Guarantee Notice: the withdrawal function and legal guarantee notice EU shops need.

For developers

Filters: pcsh_status (the open/closed state), pcsh_now, pcsh_settings_fields.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin (WooCommerce must be active).
  2. Go to WooCommerce > Settings > Store hours.
  3. Tick “Close now” or set the vacation dates, adjust the notice and save. The status at the top shows whether the shop is open.
sections.faq:
Do customers still see my products?

Yes. Only purchasing is paused. Product pages, categories and search stay as they are.

What about orders that are already placed?

They are not affected. You can process them as usual.

My shop still looks open to some visitors

If you use a page cache, clear it after closing or reopening, or exclude shop pages from the cache.

Which time zone is used?

The time zone under Settings > General.

Can I keep taking orders and just show a notice?

Yes. Set “While closed” to show the notice only. Customers can still order and see that orders ship after you return.

Can I set regular weekly opening hours?

The free plugin handles closures and vacations. Weekly opening hours (for example Monday to Friday, 9:00 to 17:00, including hours past midnight) and multiple planned closures are in the optional Pro add-on.
